subject: Concierge live: streaming parse throttle causing p99 latency & errors
messages:
From: Alicia Trent <alicia.trent@checkoutlabs.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: Concierge live - sudden p99 jump and 502 errors

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing a sharp latency spike and a stream of 502/504 errors on the Concierge live integration around 08:45 PDT. P99 jumped from ~230ms to >2.5s and error rate climbed from 0.4% to ~7%. This is impacting checkout conversions and we have dozens of users affected.

Our team captured a few gateway traces and a snippet of the client connection logs where requests stall during header reassembly. Attaching two files.

Attached: concierge_error_snippet.log (text), gateway-trace-20270505.txt (text)

We urgently need a workaround (even something temporary) and ETA for a fix. Can we get a postmortem and an exec point of contact?

Thanks,
Alicia Trent
Head of Integrations, Checkout Labs
Alicia.Trent@checkoutlabs.com

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: Concierge live - sudden p99 jump and 502 errors

Team — initial triage notes:
- Replayed checkoutlabs gateway trace in staging; able to reproduce stalls when header blocks exceed ~12KB and connections arrive at ~120–160rps.
- The streaming parser's header reassembly path appears to back off aggressively under continuous small-chunk arrivals; the dechunker state machine holds buffers and delays callback invocation until a high-water mark is reached which increases tail latency.
- There is also a queueing effect in our ingress worker pool: retry bursts cause worker starvation which amplifies the parser stalling.

Short mitigation candidate (low-risk): apply a temporary lower watermark for header callback (force earlier callback on partial headers) and add a short-lived admission throttle that smooths bursts from a single IP. This is a code change but patchable and can be rolled back quickly.

I'll prepare a patch and test it in staging now. If we can get a safe patch, we can push to a canary pool and give Checkout Labs a temporary dial-back to their problematic streams.

Neha
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Patch ready for canary: header-callback-low-watermark

Patch status update:
- I pushed a patch branch (ingest/low-watermark-callback) that forces the parser to emit a header-callback when accumulated header bytes exceed 4KB instead of waiting for higher thresholds. This reduces head-of-line buffering in most of our repros.
- Added a short-lived admission smoothing flag (request_smooth=true) we can gate via config per tenant.
- Unit + integration tests pass in staging; reproduced client trace now shows p99 improvement from >2.5s to ~310ms in canary. Error rate drops to <1%.
- Risk: minimal functional change but may surface rare partial-header parsing edgecases; I've added defensive validation.

Requesting approval to deploy to a small canary pool (5% of Checkout Labs traffic) and to enable request_smooth flag for them.

Neha

If the canary holds for 30–45 minutes we'll widen the rollout. We can also schedule a call now with your on-call to walk through the mitigation steps.

Subject: Re: Production: Concierge live - sudden p99 jump and 502 errors — follow-up and next steps

Alicia — final update for today:
- Rollout: engineering widened the patch to 100% of your traffic at 15:40 PDT after a successful 45-minute canary. Post-rollout telemetry shows sustained p99 ~300–420ms and error rate <0.9%.
- Root cause (working title): interaction between recent client header framing from Checkout Labs (more frequent small-header chunks) and our streaming parser's previous high-water buffer policy which produced backpressure and worker starvation under bursty traffic.
- Action items:
  1) Engineering will harden the parser path to remove the high-water stall condition and add more deterministic backpressure signals (ETA: 48 hours).
  2) We'll collaborate offline on a recommended SDK patch for Checkout Labs to reduce small-header fragmentation; Neha will share notes.
  3) CS will prepare a postmortem within 24 hours and a credit proposal if reasonable for impacted requests.

Attachments and links included above. If you want an executive sync tomorrow please propose times — Grace is on copy for escalation.

Thank you for your patience and for the quick logs that helped reproduction. We'll follow up with a formal SOC-style postmortem and timeline for the permanent fix.

— Rishi
Director, Customer Escalations
Redwood Inference
